staleness_predicate: For every dev/plans/runs/STATUS-0.8.*.md board that is NOT already banner-marked 'CLOSED — historical record' in its first 15 lines (a header-region scan wide enough to survive T3's YAML frontmatter, which pushes the banner to line 10 on at least one real board; closed boards are frozen and nothing lands into them again, so they are never scanned and cannot false-positive), parse the release version from the filename, then walk `git log <tip>` (default tip=HEAD; no pathspec, since `git log -- <path>` prunes --no-ff merge commits via default history simplification) newest-first for commits whose subject matches this repo's own landing convention `merge(<version>): Slice[- ]<N> ...`. Because the walk is newest-first, only the FIRST (i.e. most recent) commit seen per slice number is checked — a superseded intermediate partial-merge for the same slice is intentionally not re-required once a newer land for that slice exists, so only the live state must be reflected. For each slice's current landing commit, its short SHA (first 8 hex chars) must appear as a literal substring somewhere in the board file; if it does not, that is a demonstrable contradiction (the commit is an ancestor of the tip by git's own history, yet the board that should record it never mentions it) and is a HARD fail. This is a floor, not a semantic reader of prose ('LANDED'/'IN FLIGHT' wording) — the real STATUS-0.8.20.md board's own SUPERSEDED-banner convention around historical 'not landed' text shows free-text wording is unsafe to regex over; requiring the literal SHA is something a board cannot satisfy without genuinely being touched at land time, which is exactly the incident (board silent for 4 days after two real merges). No network; two small file/commit scans; cheap. Known scope limit: only recognizes the `merge(0.8.z): Slice[- ]N` subject convention used by the one currently-live board (0.8.20); older/closed boards used other merge-subject shapes but are skipped anyway (banner-closed), so this does not affect them — if a future release adopts a different convention, the fix is to extend this one regex, not add a second predicate implementation.

deviations: The design doc's item 2 sketch (§8) suggested an explicit `--slice N --sha <sha>` invocation shape mirroring --expect-closed. I implemented a tip-wide ancestry sweep instead (scripts/check-board-currency.sh --tip <ref>, no --slice/--sha args) because the task brief explicitly reprioritized this ('the staleness predicate is yours to design... prefer failing on a demonstrable contradiction... over a heuristic that will produce false positives') and a flag-driven single-slice check cannot be reused unmodified by the CI job (item 3), which has no single slice/sha to name and must sweep the whole board against ancestry. One predicate, two callers, as item 3 requires ('do not write the logic twice').

Found and fixed one predicate bug before it shipped: git log with a pathspec (`-- .`) silently prunes --no-ff merge commits via default history simplification (a merge commit whose tree is TREESAME to a parent — exactly what --landing merges are — becomes invisible). Removed the pathspec; documented the trap inline in check-board-currency.sh.

Found and fixed a second predicate bug before it shipped: the closed-banner header scan was originally `head -n 5`, which misses STATUS-0.8.9.1.md's real CLOSED banner (pushed to line 10 by T3's YAML frontmatter block) — that board would have been wrongly treated as 'live' and scanned. Widened to `head -n 15` (still a header-region scan, not whole-file, to avoid a live board's own prose about a sibling closed board false-matching) and added Fixture C2 / Arm 3b as a permanent regression guard reproducing the exact frontmatter shape.
